LESSON: TIME, DISTANCE, AND SPEED

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements 3.4 Volume and Capacity (8 lessons) • metre cube (m3 ) as a unit of
Topic 3.5: Time, Distance, and Speed
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Time, Distance, and Speed, part of Measurements 3.4 Volume and Capacity (8 lessons) • metre cube (m3 ) as a unit of in Grade 7 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: Why do we relate distance, time and speed? 2. What is the importance of speed in daily activities?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify units of measuring time in real- life situations

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Time, Distance, and Speed in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. convert units of time from one form to another in learning situations

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Time, Distance, and Speed in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. convert units of measuring distance in learning situations

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Time, Distance, and Speed in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. identify speed as distance covered per unit time in different situations

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Time, Distance, and Speed in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. work out speed in km/h and m/s in real-life situations

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Time, Distance, and Speed in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. convert units of speed from kilometers per hour (Km/

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Time, Distance, and Speed in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

H. to meters per second (m/

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Time, Distance, and Speed in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

S. and vice versa in real-life

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Time, Distance, and Speed in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

A. identify units of measuring time in real- life situations

   Time, Distance, and Speed helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

   Time, Distance, and Speed helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

   Time, Distance, and Speed helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

H. and vice versa in real-life

I. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use analog or digital clock to tell time in hours, minutes, and seconds and discuss the units of time

2. create a conversion table on units of time

3. discuss and estimate distances between two or more points and convert distances in Km to meters and vice versa

4. engage in activities that involve distance and time such as track events to relate time, distance, and speed

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use analog or digital clock to tell time in hours, minutes, and seconds and discuss the units of time
2. create a conversion table on units of time
3. discuss and estimate distances between two or more points and convert distances in Km to meters and vice versa
4. engage in activities that involve distance and time such as track events to relate time, distance, and speed

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Time, Distance, and Speed together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and Problem-solving: as the learner creates conversion tables relate and determine distance, time, and

speed.

● Self-efficacy: as the learner observes punctuality in attending to different activities.

Values

● Patriotism: as the learner observes road safety rules including speed limits for crossing the roads.

● Integrity: as the learner observes punctuality and work out correct distances.
